title: fix(runtime)!: REST's /actions door resolves a standalone action through the protocol's by-name read, so a disabled package's object-less action answers the "no declaration" 404 instead of running
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuXquM9v2r8ymXj6TzynfjMF)_

Fixes #25308

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6353801421

REST's `POST /api/v1/actions/global/NAME` (and its empty-segment spelling `/actions//NAME`) no longer runs an object-less action whose owning package is disabled. `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` now reads a standalone action through the protocol's by-name `action` read, in `readExposureDeclaration`'s shape (`getMetaItemForExecution`, else `getMetaItem`; `{ type: 'action', name }`; the item under its own name or nothing; `ownsRoute` kept). That read withholds a disabled package's item, as `GET /api/v1/meta/action/NAME` does, so such an action resolves to no declaration and the door answers its existing ADR-0110 D3 "no declaration" `404`: the same status, code and message, but for the name, that a name nothing declares gets. The registry and metadata-service copies are read only on a host whose protocol has no by-name read. The answer is the one ruling 6353801421 on the card chose (letter B).

## The defect, measured on base `258f4e6aa`

#25296 (PR #25305) refuses an action on an object of a disabled package `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, and skips object-less keys by design: they name no object to ask about. The declaration resolution then read the engine registry's `action` items (else the metadata service's rows), where a disabled package's items stay, so an object-less action resolved and dispatched. It resolves on an object route too, because `ownsRoute` accepts an object-less owner on any route, and so does a package's top-level action bound to another, enabled package's object (the registry's `boundCodeActions` leaves it off that object, so the embedded read misses and the standalone read found it).

Real kernels (`ObjectKernel` + `MetadataPlugin` + `ObjectQLPlugin` over a better-sqlite3 `SqlDriver`), in the two shapes #25296's pin file already boots (`env_local` with `createStandaloneStack`'s options, and no `environmentId`), driven through the runtime dispatcher's `dispatch()`. The fixture package gains a top-level action with no `objectName` (`type: 'script'`, its handler registered under `global`) and a top-level action bound to a second, enabled package's object; the environment authors one object-less action through `protocol.saveMetaItem`.

| request, as a signed-in caller, the package disabled | base, both shapes | this PR, both shapes |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `GET /meta/action/NAME`'s read (`protocol.getMetaItem`, unchanged) | `item` withheld | same |
| `POST /actions/global/NAME` | **`200 { pong: 'package' }`, the handler ran** | the "no declaration" `404` |
| `POST /actions//NAME` | **`200`, the handler ran** | the "no declaration" `404` |
| `POST /actions/ENABLED_OBJECT/NAME` (the object-less action on an enabled object's route) | **`200`, the handler ran** | the "no declaration" `404` |
| `POST /actions/ENABLED_OBJECT/BOUND` (the package's action bound to the enabled package's object) | **`200`, the handler ran** | the "no declaration" `404` |
| the environment-authored object-less action, both spellings | `200` | `200` |
| `POST /actions/global/NAME`, anonymous | `401` | `401` |
| the package's action, both spellings, after `registry.enablePackage` | `200` | `200` |

## The ruling's precondition (item 7), measured before the change

With every package ENABLED, on both shapes, both protocol faces (`getMetaItemForExecution` and `getMetaItem`) served under its own name every standalone action the old sources resolved, and REST answered each `200`: a manifest-registered object-less action and a manifest-registered bound action (`_packageId` in the registry), an environment-authored object-less action (no `_packageId`), and a compiled artifact's object-less actions, the project's own (`AppPlugin` over `loadArtifactBundle`, no `_packageId`) and its `packages[]` entry's. With those packages disabled, both faces withheld the packaged ones (`item` absent, envelope `packageId` the disabled package) and still served the authored and the project's own. Scratch probe, not committed; no enabled, declared action was missing from the protocol read, so no fork was raised.

## What changed

- **`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`.** `resolveRouteActionDeclaration`: after the object's embedded actions (unchanged), a standalone declaration comes from the protocol's by-name `action` read when the `protocol` slot has one. A read that throws is the metadata plane failing to answer: `degraded`, so the door's existing `503`, ⛔ never a fall-back to a copy, which would run a disabled package's action during the outage. The registry and metadata-service sources stay, below, for a host whose protocol has no by-name read. No runtime call of `isPackageDisabled`, no `_packageId` read, no copy of the protocol's predicate. Signature unchanged; nothing newly published.
- **`.changeset/25308-rest-global-actions-disabled-package.md`.** A `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; both declaration lines are in the body.

`domains/actions.ts` is unchanged: its "no declaration" `404` answers the absent declaration as it answers any other.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes, old to new, where the `protocol` slot has a by-name read and the action the route names is not embedded in the route's object:

1. **`POST /actions/global/NAME` or `/actions//NAME`, NAME a disabled package's object-less script action.** Old: `200`, its handler's result (the body ran). New: the "no declaration" `404`; the handler is not called.
2. **`POST /actions/OBJECT/NAME`, OBJECT an enabled object, NAME a disabled package's object-less action.** Old: `200`, the handler ran. New: the "no declaration" `404`.
3. **`POST /actions/OBJECT/NAME`, NAME a disabled package's top-level action bound to OBJECT of an enabled package.** Old: dispatched. New: the "no declaration" `404`.
4. **Any of 1 to 3 gated by `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks, switched off in the activation ledger, a declarative update or a `flow` action.** Old: `403`, `409 ACTION_DISABLED`, the record load's answer, or a dispatch. New: the "no declaration" `404`. Not pinned separately: the resolution answers before every gate that reads the declaration, by construction.
5. **The protocol's by-name read throws.** Old: the registry's copy (else the metadata service's) answered, and the action ran. New: the door's `503` ("the metadata plane is unavailable … Refusing rather than running it ungated"). Not pinned: no rig here makes that read throw.
6. **The activation door, `POST /actions/_activation/OBJECT/NAME`, on a disabled package's standalone action.** It resolves through the same function. Old: a ledger row was written. New: that door's own "no declaration" `404` ("there is nothing to switch"). Derived from the shared resolution, not pinned. Re-enable the package to switch it.
7. **A standalone action whose environment row overrides a code one.** The protocol's layered read serves the merged item (environment row over code), where the registry copy served the code item. Derived, not pinned; the probe above found no enabled action where the two disagree on presence.

Unchanged: the anonymous baseline (`401`) and the `405` stay first; an action on an object of a disabled package still answers #25296's `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` first; an object's embedded actions resolve as before; an enabled package's object-less actions and an environment-authored one run as before (pinned on both shapes and spellings); re-enabling the package restores its actions at once, because nothing records the answer (pinned); a host whose protocol has no by-name read. The cost is one by-name protocol read per invocation of a standalone action, the read `/meta/action/NAME` makes.

## Pins

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-disabled-package.test.ts`, extended from 24 to 50 cases on real kernels.** The fixture gains the object-less action and its handler under `global`, an environment-authored object-less action, an optional enabled side package, and (with it) the package's action bound to the side package's object. Per shape:

- **ENABLED control.** The package's and the authored object-less actions answer `200` with their handlers' results on both spellings. An object-less name nothing declares answers the "no declaration" `404`.
- **DISABLED package.** Precondition: the protocol's by-name read withholds the package's action and serves the authored one. On both spellings, the package's action answers exactly what `qa_nowhere` answers (status, code and message with the name taken out). The handler is never called, and `getData`, `updateData` and `executeAction` are never reached. The same holds on the enabled side package's object route, and for the package's action bound to that object. The authored action still answers `200` on both spellings. The anonymous caller still answers `401`. After `enablePackage`, the package's action runs again on both spellings.

**Red before, green after.** The directions were predicted before each run, under the verify lock. The test imports the runtime's source, so no `dist/` is involved.

| leg | mutation | result | which failed |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| main | base's `action-execution.ts` and `domains/actions.ts` (`git restore --source=258f4e6a`, worktree only), restored by `git checkout HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty | 8 failed, 42 passed | the four DISABLED leak cases (two spellings, the enabled object's route, the cross-package bound action) on both shapes, each `expected 200 to be 404` |
| fix | the protocol read skipped (`if (byName) {` to `if (byName && false) {` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, blob `e4eebd83e059` to `271f6b423b30`; restored blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty) | 8 failed, 42 passed | the same eight |
| none | none | 50 passed | none |

The existing action-door suites (`action-activation-*`, `actions-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger`, `anonymous-gate-actions-automation`, `tenancy-posture-outage-gates`, `scoped-service-miss-attribution`, `actions-every-verb.hono.integration`, `action-governance-scope-divergence`, `meta-overlay-read-your-writes`) are in that count, unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- **The coded answer.** The card's Shape asked for "the same coded answer #25296 chooses, reusing the same package-disabled read". For an `action` item the two cannot both hold. #25296's read is the by-name OBJECT read, which throws `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. The by-name ACTION read throws nothing: it withholds the item. The choice went to the coordinator as `needs_decision`, and ruling 6353801421 chose the read's own answer (absent: the D3 `404`, no hint, no package code, no new code). This PR implements that ruling as written.
- **An interim implementation was replaced, not shipped.** Before the ruling arrived, this branch asked `registry.isPackageDisabled(action._packageId)` at the door (commit `57b21c61`). The ruling forbids that read (item 2), and `e30b5e80` reverts it. The squash carries only the protocol read.
- **Branch name.** This PR's branch is `claude/project-thread-vlqmr4`, the name the session was given, not `claude/issue-25308-…`; the Duplicate Fix Guard may say so. The claim (comment 6353642578) names it.
